cards.name: Sticker cut-out with white outline and drop shadow
cards.summary: The subject cut out of its photo with a thick white sticker border and a soft shadow, so it looks like a die-cut sticker lifted off the page.
use_for: social posts and stories with a cut-out subject
avoid: thin, wispy edges (hair, fur): a white outline makes the mask flaws obvious; refine the mask or simplify the outline
a busy background colour close to white: the border disappears; add a darker backdrop
cutter (die-cut) files: they need a real vector path, so use the Illustrator or CorelDRAW plan and expand the result

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: a non-destructive cut-out mask (skip it if Select and Mask already output a mask).

effects.note: Layer Style > Stroke on the cut-out layer: Outside, 16 px white (the render at 10 px showed the outside position rounds the outer corners, which suits a sticker).
Layer Style > Drop Shadow: 35 % black Multiply, 8 px down-right (light at 135 degrees, upper left, as the render showed), Size 14 for a soft lift.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).

On a new fill added below the art in the Appearance panel (white), Effect > Path > Offset Path 10 pt: the fill grows into a sticker border around vector art or traced type. jntp 2 rendered miter corners; the round-join code (0 or 1) was not identified in the harvest, so check the corners.
Effect > Stylize > Drop Shadow on the whole object: 4 pt right and down, blur 6, 35 % Multiply. Untested: no render frame exists for it (verdict not_rendered), so this caps the recipe at medium.
Optional: Object > Expand Appearance to turn the border into a real path for a cutter file.

Effects > Contour on the vector shape or the traced silhouette (see manual steps): Outside (Direction 1), one step, Offset 0.08 in document units, white fill and outline, round corners (CornerType 2); the render showed outside rings around a star.
Drop Shadow on the contour group: flat, 35 %, feather 10, a small offset down-right (negative Y is down), Multiply merge (9), as in the render.

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.

Illustrator / CorelDRAW with a photo cut-out: vectorise the silhouette first (Illustrator Object > Image Trace > Make with a Silhouettes preset, then Expand; CorelDRAW Bitmaps > Quick Trace, then Object > Shaping > Weld the traced pieces), give it the white contour or offset, and place the photo on top.
cards.note: Photoshop plan: every visual step render-verified (Stroke, Drop Shadow pass) and Select > Subject verified live; Illustrator's Drop Shadow has no render yet.

cards.name: Glowing outline around the subject
cards.summary: A coloured neon-style halo traced around the cut-out subject, optionally with a thin crisp line, to make it jump off a dark background.
use_for: event and nightlife posters on dark backgrounds
highlighting one person or product in a group shot
avoid: light backgrounds: a bright glow vanishes on white; use a dark backdrop or a dark glow
Screen-mode glows over light areas: Screen can only lighten
glow colours that clash with skin: cyan, magenta and yellow read as neon; orange-red reads as fire

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: a non-destructive cut-out mask (skip it if Select and Mask already output a mask).

effects.note: Layer Style > Outer Glow on the cut-out layer: cyan #00E5FF, 90 %, Spread 10, Size 30 (the render at 15 / 40 gave a soft halo all round with no offset). Normal mode works on any background; Screen only on dark ones.
Layer Style > Stroke, Outside 3 px in a near-white tint of the glow colour: the hot core of a neon line.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).

Effect > Stylize > Outer Glow on vector art or traced type: Normal (blnd 0), 24 pt, full opacity (the render at 30 pt gave a clear cyan halo). The glow colour (sclr) was not proven to round-trip by script: set it in the dialog or with a graphic style if it comes out black.

Drop Shadow used as a glow: flat, no offset, cyan, 90 %, feather 25, Normal merge (0). The render used a black offset shadow; zero offset and a bright colour are not render-tested, so judge on screen.

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.
Illustrator with a photo: trace the silhouette (Image Trace) and put the glow on the traced shape behind the photo; on a placed image the glow follows the image bounds, not the subject.
cards.note: Photoshop plan render-verified (Outer Glow, Stroke pass); the CorelDRAW zero-offset glow is not.

cards.name: Background blur (portrait-mode bokeh)
cards.summary: The subject stays sharp while the background goes softly out of focus with bright highlights blooming into bokeh discs, like a wide-aperture lens.
use_for: portraits shot on a phone or at a small aperture
product shots with a distracting background
making space for type behind the subject
avoid: a background so close to the subject that real blur would be small: heavy blur looks fake; keep Iris Radius modest
hair and fine edges: blur bleeds the subject into the background unless the subject is removed from the blurred copy first (the Content-Aware step below)
news photos: faking depth of field is an edit; disclose it if required

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Layer > Duplicate Layer.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection on the copy (the top layer): the sharp subject layer.
Make the original layer below active (app.activeDocument.activeLayer = the lower layer) and Select > Subject again: the background layer is cleaned next.
Select > Modify > Expand 8 px so the fill also covers the subject's halo.
Edit > Content-Aware Fill on the original: verified live, it fills with texture from the surroundings onto a new layer, so the subject's colours are gone from the background before it is blurred.
Layer > Merge Layers with the fill layer and the original selected: one clean background layer.
Select > Deselect.

Filter > Blur > Lens Blur on the cleaned background: no depth map (BkDi None), hexagon iris, Iris Radius 25, Blade Curvature 30 for rounder discs, Specular Brightness 20 / Threshold 230 so only real highlights bloom, Noise 2 to match the photo's grain (the render at 50 / 40 / 200 / 0 defocused evenly with blooming highlights).

On a duplicate of the bitmap placed behind the original: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur, Radius 120 (the dialog maximum 250 already gave only a light blur on a 1920 px photo, so expect a soft rather than a heavy blur).

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.
CorelDRAW: there is no automatic subject selection; draw a path around the subject by hand and PowerClip the sharp original into it (Object > PowerClip), over the blurred copy.
Photoshop alternative with more control: Filter > Blur Gallery > Iris Blur or Field Blur by hand (no script route harvested).

cards.name: Thumbnail punch
cards.summary: YouTube-style thumbnail treatment: punchy colour and clarity, a cut-out subject with a bold outline and rim-light glow, and a darkened background so the subject reads at tiny sizes.
avoid: over-saturating skin: keep Vibrance (not Saturation) for the boost
outline colours that match the background: pick a contrasting outline (white or yellow on dark, black on light)
text over the face: place type beside the subject, never across it

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Layer > Duplicate Layer while the subject is selected; the copy is the active layer and the selection stays.
Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: a non-destructive cut-out mask (skip it if Select and Mask already output a mask).

effects.note: Layer Style > Stroke on the subject layer (the top copy): Outside 10 px white (or #FFE600 yellow).
Layer Style > Outer Glow: white, Screen, 70 %, Size 25: a rim light that separates the subject from the background.
Layer Style > Drop Shadow: 50 % black, 6 px, Size 18.

steps.note: One layer style: these 3 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Make the original (background) layer active and add an Exposure adjustment layer: it lands between the background and the subject layer, so -0.7 stops darkens only the background.
Make the subject layer active, then a Clarity and dehaze layer on top of the stack (it grades subject and background): crisp detail that survives downscaling (render at 60 / 50 was strong).
Color and vibrance layer on top: Vibrance +35, Saturation +10.
Brightness/Contrast layer on top: +8 / +20.
Effects > Adjust > Vibrance on the photo.
Effects > Sharpen > Unsharp Mask for thumbnail crispness.
Effects > Contour outside, one white step, on the traced subject silhouette placed behind the photo cut-out (see manual steps).
Drop Shadow on the outlined subject.

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.
CorelDRAW: cut the subject out by hand (draw a path round it and PowerClip the photo into it, or trace a silhouette with Bitmaps > Quick Trace + Weld) before the contour step.
Check the thumbnail at its real display size (about 320 px wide): if the subject does not read, push the outline and background darkening further.
cards.note: Photoshop plan: every visual step render-verified; the CorelDRAW plan depends on a hand-made cut-out.

cards.name: Subject on a flat colour background
cards.summary: The photo's background replaced by one flat brand colour behind the cut-out subject: clean, graphic and on-brand.
use_for: product tiles for marketplaces and catalogues
avoid: background colours close to skin or clothing colours: the cut-out edge disappears
rough masks: a flat background shows every halo; refine with Select and Mask or Layer > Matting > Defringe

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Select > Inverse: the background is selected.

Layer > New Fill Layer > Solid Color in the brand colour while the background is selected: the fill layer's mask comes from the selection, so it covers only the background (the card notes a fill layer fills the active selection through its mask).

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.
To let the subject float, select the subject again, duplicate the photo layer, Reveal Selection on the copy, move it above the fill layer and give it a soft Drop Shadow (distance 0, Size 30, 25 %).
Clean a light halo along the edge with Layer > Matting > Defringe 1-2 px or Remove White Matte on the cut-out layer.
CorelDRAW / Illustrator: draw the background rectangle in the brand colour and place a Photoshop cut-out (PNG or PSD with transparency) on top; neither app selects a subject automatically.

cards.name: Hard offset shadow (pop sticker)
cards.summary: A solid, unblurred shadow offset down-right behind a cut-out, logo or type: the flat comic / pop-art sticker look.
use_for: bold social graphics and promo tiles
cut-out subjects on flat colour backgrounds
avoid: photographic or soft lighting scenes: a hard shadow looks graphic, not real
very long offsets on small items: they read as a second object

effects.note: Layer Style > Drop Shadow on the cut-out or type layer: 100 % opacity, Spread 100 and Size 0 make a solid copy, Distance 14 px down-right (light at 135 degrees). Colour #1A1A1A or a dark brand colour; Normal mode for a flat colour.
Optional Layer Style > Stroke, Outside 6 px in the same dark colour, for the comic outline.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).

On an extra fill below the art in the Appearance panel (dark colour), Effect > Distort & Transform > Transform with one copy moved 6 pt right and 6 pt down (moveV is in Illustrator's effect coordinates; check the direction on screen): a solid offset copy behind (the render showed copies stepping right and down).
Drop Shadow: flat, 100 %, Feather 0 (FeatherEdge flat), offset down-right, Normal merge: a solid offset shadow. The render used feather 12 / 75 %; zero feather is not render-tested.

cards.note: Photoshop plan render-verified (Drop Shadow, Stroke pass); the Illustrator and CorelDRAW settings differ from their rendered demos.

cards.name: Photo frame with border and shadow
cards.summary: A photo given a white print border (even, or deeper at the bottom like an instant print) and a soft shadow so it sits on the layout like a real print.
avoid: frames thinner than about 3 % of the photo width: they read as a hairline, not a print border
heavy shadows on a white page: keep them soft and short

steps.note: Image > Canvas Size on the photo (still a Background layer): add the border, e.g. +6 % width and height, anchor centre; for an instant-print frame add extra height and anchor top. The new area takes the canvas extension colour (white).
Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Image > Canvas Size again, transparent this time (the layer is no longer Background): room for the shadow.
Layer Style > Drop Shadow on the framed photo: 30 %, 10 px, Size 20.
On a white rectangle drawn at the photo's bounds and placed behind it, Effect > Path > Offset Path 12 pt: the even white border, miter corners (jntp 2, as rendered).
Effect > Stylize > Drop Shadow on the white rectangle: 30 % Multiply. Untested: no render frame (verdict not_rendered), which caps the recipe at medium.
Draw a rectangle (white fill, no outline) slightly inside the photo size, Object > PowerClip > Create Empty PowerClip Frame, then place the photo into it (contents.AddToPowerClip).
Effects > Contour outside on the frame, one white step: the border (mitered corners, CornerType 3).
Drop Shadow on the contour group: 30 %, feather 15.

manual_steps: Rotate the framed photo a few degrees by hand for a casual scattered-prints look.

cards.name: Circular avatar with ring
cards.summary: A head-and-shoulders photo cropped into a circle with a coloured ring around it: the profile-picture and speaker-card style.
avoid: cropping too tight: leave space above the head and show the shoulders
thin rings at small sizes: below about 4 % of the diameter they vanish in feeds

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.

With a circular selection made over the photo (Elliptical Marquee by hand, or app.activeDocument.selection.select() with the circle's points), Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: the circular crop.

effects.note: Layer Style > Stroke, Outside 12 px in the brand colour: the ring follows the circular mask.
Layer Style > Drop Shadow, soft and short.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Draw a circle over the placed photo, select both, Object > Clipping Mask > Make (confirmed in the harvest): the circular crop.
Copy the circle, give it the ring colour as a stroke-less fill, place it behind the clipped photo and apply Effect > Path > Offset Path 6 pt: a ring 6 pt wide shows around the photo.
Draw a circle, Object > PowerClip > Create Empty PowerClip Frame, then place the photo into it.
Effects > Contour outside on the frame circle, one step in the ring colour.

manual_steps: Centre the face in the circle by hand (move the photo inside the mask, clipping group or PowerClip).

cards.name: Type behind the subject
cards.summary: A big headline placed behind the person or product, with the cut-out subject layered back on top, for a magazine-cover depth effect.
avoid: covering so much of the headline that it cannot be read: keep the key word clear of the subject
busy subject edges (hair) over thin type: refine the mask

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background: the locked Background becomes an ordinary layer that can take a mask and layer styles.
Select > Subject (executeAction 'autoCutout', sampleAllLayers false): Adobe's automatic subject detection, verified live (selection created).
Layer > Duplicate Layer with the subject selected, then Reveal Selection on the copy (next step): the subject-only layer, moved to the top of the stack.
Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: a non-destructive cut-out mask (skip it if Select and Mask already output a mask).
Optional Layer Style > Drop Shadow on the subject layer, distance 0, Size 25: a soft separation from the type behind.

manual_steps: If Select > Subject misses part of the subject (several people, products held in hands, busy backgrounds), fix the mask by hand: paint white / black on the layer mask, or select with the Object Selection Tool first.
Set the headline as a type layer between the original photo and the subject layer (Type Tool by hand, or app.activeDocument.artLayers.add() with kind TEXT and move it below the subject layer).
CorelDRAW / Illustrator: stack the same three layers (photo, text, a Photoshop cut-out PNG) in the object order; neither app cuts out the subject automatically.
